entities.summary: Ippolito de' Medici, the illegitimate son of Giuliano di Lorenzo de' Medici, played a significant role in the early 16th-century banking and political landscape of Florence, Italy. Born around 1500 to Pacifica Brandano, his mistress, Ippolito's life was marked by his involvement in the Medici family's banking and political machinations. He worked closely with his half-brother, Lorenzo de' Medici, and later his half-brother-in-law, Cosimo de' Medici, in managing the family's vast financial interests and power. Ippolito's actions contributed to the Medici family's continued dominance in Florence, solidifying their hold on the city's politics and economy. His legacy, however, was largely overshadowed by that of his more prominent half-brothers, leaving behind a relatively minor yet fascinating footnote in the annals of Medici history.
